problem: Training-free object navigation methods depend on external mapping and heuristic local planners rather than true spatial understanding, while learning-based VLA methods (mostly for VLN) rely on ground-truth actions and video histories. In object navigation it is unclear what counts as a high-quality expert action, so mixed-quality demonstrations are hard to use.
motivation: Object navigation requires autonomous exploration, so there are no clean ground-truth actions for behavior cloning or reward evaluation. Video histories are costly and redundant. A compact map abstraction plus value-aware training could unify noisy history and extract good exploration behavior from mixed-quality data.
key_idea: Feed a rotated top-down semantic map plus recent frames into a VLA, pretrain it for map understanding, behavior-clone it, then amplify with short-horizon return-to-go weighted BC and an expectile-regression reward head.
insight: The ablations show the map understanding pretraining (Stage 1) and reward amplification are complementary: full 3-stage gets 46.7 SR vs 38.1 for BC only. Map-description data matters most; with CoT-only Stage 1 SR collapses to 23.2, and Stage 3 recovers it to 39.6. Reward design matters: RTG with softplus weighting beats instant reward (45.6), no weighting (43.2) and offline GRPO (31.0).
method: Semantic map: a (C+2)-channel top-down map built à la SemExp from RGB-D, pose and segmentation, enlarged and rotated so the agent arrow always points up
Map/observation encoding: separate map encoder and observation encoder; the previous 3 frames are aggregated by a Q-Former and concatenated with the current frame
Cross-attention fusion: observation features are the query and map features the key/value; a projector maps the result into the LLM space; the LLM outputs a 4-step action sequence via an action head
Stage 1 map understanding: 1.5M map-language pairs (rule-generated descriptions plus LLM CoT) collected with L3MVN on HM3D; trains map encoder, projector and full LLM
Stage 2 behavior cloning: 0.73M samples with cross-entropy on the next 4 actions; map and observation encoders frozen; stop actions augmented

Stage 3 reward amplification: 0.54M extra samples; reward is the z-normalized goal-distance reduction over 4 actions; loss is softplus(RTG)*BC + λ*expectile regression of RTG; reward head discarded at inference

setting.backbone: Multimodal LLM VLA (LLM fully fine-tuned) with map encoder, observation encoder, Q-Former and cross-attention fusion
setting.training_data: HM3D 75 train scenes; L3MVN-collected data: 1.5M map-language pairs (Stage 1), 0.73M BC samples (Stage 2), 0.54M reward samples (Stage 3)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB frames (current + 3 history) plus semantic map built from RGB-D, pose and segmentation
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions, predicted as a sequence of 4 steps (including stop)
setting.privileged: semantic map construction uses depth, pose and semantic segmentation; ground-truth distance to goal is used for training rewards only

numbers.extra: trained on HM3D train scenes with L3MVN-collected data
trained only on HM3D, directly tested on Gibson
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Gibson Success 71.0, SPL 21.0→41.1; * zero-shot on Gibson

numbers_note: HM3D split is stated as 20 validation scenes; the Gibson val split is stated as 1,000 episodes across 5 scenes.
results: MUVLA reaches 46.7 SR / 21.0 SPL on HM3D, +12.1 SR over MapNav (34.6), and 71.0 SR / 41.1 SPL zero-shot on Gibson, above SemExp (65.2 / 33.6). MapNav has a higher HM3D SPL (25.6).
limitations: Only SR and SPL on HM3D and Gibson are reported, with a weaker SPL than MapNav on HM3D
Depends on an externally built semantic map (depth, pose, segmentation) and on L3MVN-collected data, so quality is bounded by that pipeline
Brittle training: exponential reward weighting collapses to 0 and CoT-only Stage 1 hurts; no real-robot tests
